name: Valparaiso University
label: Valparaiso University

pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/293490494: large area 'Valparaiso University' (2594 m across): previous pin kept, it lies inside.

text.description:
Valparaiso University is a Lutheran university in Valparaiso, Indiana, spread over a 350-acre campus. It began in 1859 as a small coeducational college and has been rebuilt and reshaped many times since. One landmark worth looking for is the Chapel of the Resurrection, dedicated in 1959 to replace a worship space lost to fire in 1956. It is one of the largest chapels on a US college campus, and it stands on the campus's highest point. That makes it easy to pick out from higher ground.

From the fourth floor you get an elevated view over the chapel and the wider campus, so you get buildings, lawns and trees in one frame. The university itself lies 147 m to the north-west of the balcony.

If you have time, two other spots are worth a look. The Resurrection Labyrinth gives the chapel's exterior with the labyrinth in the foreground. The Student Bridge is a footbridge with student names and initials carved into its metal. Keep your phone steady against the rail or your body for sharp shots, and wipe the lens before you start.
text.geographic_location: The university campus is in the city of Valparaiso, Indiana.
text.directions_text: No public transport stop is listed for this spot, so navigate to the Christopher Center Library on the campus in Valparaiso, Indiana. Go inside and take the stairs or the elevator to the fourth floor, then step out onto the balcony. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the whole campus view. Switch to telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pick out the chapel. Try ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you want a lot of sky and ground in the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand at Christopher Center Library balcony (fourth floor balcony, reached by stairs or elevator from inside the library). An elevated view over the chapel and the wider campus. It is reached by stairs or the elevator from inside the library.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and place the chapel on one of the upper crossing points, with trees and lawns filling the lower part of the frame. Keep the phone level so the buildings do not lean. Then take one wider shot of the whole campus. For a ground-level alternative, try the Resurrection Labyrinth for the chapel with the labyrinth in front, or the Student Bridge for its carved names.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the chapel to set focus, then slide the exposure down a little if the sky is bright so the sky keeps its detail. If you shoot through glass or a rail, hold the phone close to it and avoid reflections.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: The balcony is open only while the sun is up and the weather permits, so go in daylight and check the weather before you climb up.

text.access_note: The balcony is inside a university library building and is reached through it, so check the official site before you go to confirm current access.

label: Chapel of the Resurrec

text.description: The Chapel of the Resurrection is the centrepiece of the Valparaiso University campus in Indiana, and it is a Northwest Indiana landmark, clearly visible from U.S. Route 30 and across the surrounding community. It stands on the highest ground on campus, so it works as a landmark in wider campus shots. Work began in 1956 and the chapel was dedicated in 1959. The chancel is circular and about 30 m high, and the apse roof is shaped like a nine-pointed star, which gives you an unusual outline to look for. Inside, the stained glass windows are about 29 m tall, designed by Peter Dohmen. The Brandt Campanile, a 44 m bell tower, stands to the south-west of the chapel. A circular prayer labyrinth was added on the east side in 2005. It makes a good foreground for a shot of the chapel's outside walls. For a different view, the balcony of the Christopher Center Library gives a raised look at the chapel with the campus laid out around it. That helps if you want to show how the building sits among the other university buildings. If you would rather get close, the labyrinth gives a low, open foreground. Inside, the tall windows reward a few minutes of looking, but this is a working chapel, so be quick and discreet if a service or rehearsal is under way.
text.geographic_location: The chapel is on the campus of Valparaiso University in the city of Valparaiso, Indiana, on the highest ground on the campus. The library balcony view is on the East Quad side, across from the University Center for the Arts.
text.directions_text: No train or bus stops are listed nearby, so start from the centre of Valparaiso and get to the university campus by car or on foot. From there the chapel lies to the north-east, about 2 minutes on foot. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) from the balcony to show the chapel with the campus around it. Try 2x or 3x if your phone has it to pick out the star-shaped roof and tower. Use the ultra-wide (0.5x) at the labyrinth or inside the chapel to fit in the tall windows.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand at Christopher Center Library balcony (balcony, off the East Quad). A raised, bird's-eye view of the chapel within the surrounding campus. The chapel is to the north-east, and from the balcony you get a raised, bird's-eye view of it within the surrounding campus. If you want the chapel's outside walls with the labyrinth in front, walk over to the Resurrection Labyrinth as an alternative.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on the gridlines and put the chapel on one of the vertical lines, leaving the campus buildings and paths in the lower part of the frame to show the layout. Keep the phone level so the tall walls do not lean. At the labyrinth, crouch slightly so the paths lead the eye towards the chapel.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the chapel to focus, then slide the exposure down a little if the sky is bright, so the stonework keeps its detail. Inside, tap on the windows and lower the exposure so the colours stay rich. Use night mode if the interior is dim, and hold the phone steady against a rail or wall.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: The balcony is open only while the sun is up and the weather allows, so plan a daytime visit. For the interior, avoid service times, when photography may be limited.

text.access_note: The chapel is a working place of worship on a university campus, and the library balcony is open only in daylight and fair weather, so check the official site before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Interior light in a large chapel is often dim, so night mode may help.
Because the chapel is a place of worship, quiet and respectful behaviour is expected inside.
A 2x or 3x zoom on a phone can bring a distant building closer without moving.

name: Porter County Courthouse
label: Porter County Courthou
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Lincolnway' (2 web pages); placed at crossing of Lincolnway and Franklin Street (our map tiles).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/907876852: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Porter County Courthouse' (49 m across).
notes: Historic courthouse at the heart of downtown Valparaiso.

text.description:
Porter County Courthouse is the grand limestone building at the heart of Valparaiso's downtown square, and it has stood on this same site for generations. The present building dates from 1883 and measures 128 by 98 feet. It was built of Indiana limestone from Ellettsville. It originally had a square central tower of 168 feet with a clock on each side. A fire on 27 December 1934 gutted the building in freezing weather, and the tower was never rebuilt. What you see today is largely the 1937 restoration, with a lower profile than the original. That history is a nice detail for a caption.

From there you get a street-level view looking west along Lincolnway, with the trees of the courthouse square running along one side. The courthouse sits to the south-west of you and may only be partly in frame, so this view works as a streetscape with the building as part of the scene. For a full, straight-on view of the building, walk into Courthouse Square and shoot across the grounds. Together the two give you a street scene and a proper portrait of the building.
text.geographic_location: In the centre of Valparaiso, Indiana, on the downtown courthouse square beside Lincolnway. The viewpoint is at the south-east corner of the Lincolnway intersection next to the square.
text.directions_text: No station or stop is listed for this spot, so start from the centre of Valparaiso and come by taxi or hired scooter to the Lincolnway intersection beside the courthouse square. From there the courthouse is to the south-west, about 1 minute on foot. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the street view along Lincolnway. Switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) if you want the trees, the street and the building in one frame. Use telephoto (2x or more, depending on your phone) for details of the limestone walls.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand at the corner of Lincolnway and Franklin Street (corner at the southeast side of the intersection, looking west along Lincolnway). A street-level view along Lincolnway with the trees of the courthouse square on one side; the building itself may appear only partly in frame. The courthouse is to your south-west, with the square's trees on that side. Keep to the pavement and watch for traffic as you line up the shot.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and use the line of the street to lead the eye along the picture, with the trees on one side. If the building is only partly in frame, accept that and treat it as part of the street scene. For the full building, walk into Courthouse Square and shoot across the grounds instead. Keep the phone level so the walls stay upright.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the limestone to focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly if the sky is bright, so the stone does not wash out. Take a few shots in case a car or passer-by spoils one.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light usually flatters pale stone and gives the tree shadows some shape. Midday sun can look flat.

text.access_note: The street corner and the square are ordinary public spaces, but for going inside the courthouse, check the official site before you go.

name: Christopher Center
label: Christopher Center
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Christopher Center Library balcony' (1 web pages); placed at at the subject (split pin).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/297975194: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Christopher Center for Library and Information Resources' (114 m across).

text.description:
The Christopher Center is the library on the campus of Valparaiso University, in Valparaiso, Indiana. It opened as the university's fourth library and replaced the older Moellering Library, which was demolished in 2005. The building has about 105,000 square feet (9,800 m2) of space and was designed by the Chicago firm Esherick Homsey Dodge & Davis, who wanted to break the mould of the traditional institutional library. A grid-like structure along the south and east sides gives the outside its distinctive look and also works as a sunscreen.

The viewpoint is the fourth-floor balcony inside the Christopher Center. The phone icon on the map is the balcony itself, not the middle of the building. From up there you look out over the Chapel and the wider campus, not back at the library's own walls. That makes it a good place for a 'view from the library' picture that shows the building in its campus setting. A student guide to the campus lists the balcony as a favourite photo spot because of the raised view. If you want a picture of the library's outside, this is not the place for it.

Keep the shot simple. Line up the Chapel with the gridlines on, and keep the horizon level. Take a few frames at different zoom levels so you have options to choose from afterwards. Check the campus map for current access before you go.
text.geographic_location: The Christopher Center stands on the campus of Valparaiso University in Valparaiso, Indiana, close to the university Chapel. Its reading room overlooks Resurrection Meadow, south of the Chapel.
text.directions_text: No public transport stops are listed for this spot, so head to the Valparaiso University campus in Valparaiso, Indiana. Once on campus, look for the Christopher Center library and go inside. Take the stairway or the elevator to the fourth floor and find the upper balcony. Check the campus map for current access before you set off. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) to take in the sweep of the campus. Then switch to the default lens (1x) for a more natural view. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pick out the Chapel from the rest of the view.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. Stand on the fourth-floor balcony inside the Christopher Center. Find the library first and then head up to the fourth floor. From the balcony the photo shows the Chapel and the campus laid out below, not the library's outer walls. It works best as a context shot.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and place the Chapel on one of the lines. Keep the horizon level. If you want a wider view, take one frame at 0.5x and another at 1x. Choose the better one afterwards.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the Chapel to set focus, then slide the exposure down a touch if the sky looks washed out. Hold the phone with both hands against your body to keep it steady.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Go in daylight so the campus view is well lit.

text.access_note: This is a university library, so access and hours may change; check the campus map or the official site before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Lowering the exposure slightly can stop a bright sky looking washed out in a view across open campus.
Holding the phone with both hands close to the body helps reduce camera shake.

label: Downtown Valparaiso
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Central Park Plaza' (3 web pages); placed at our map tiles: 'Central Park' (pois).
pin_note: Position from Wikidata Q7912571: kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Historic Franklin Street area with shops and cafes.

text.description:
Valparaiso's downtown is a working town centre, not a museum piece. Shops, restaurants, offices and local government sit together in a compact grid of old commercial buildings. The district is anchored on the Porter County Courthouse and covers 14 blocks around the square, between Jefferson, Morgan, Monroe and Napoleon Streets. For a phone photographer the appeal is the mix: late-1800s and early-1900s commercial buildings, some in limestone, shaded pavements and a lively street scene, all within a few minutes' walk.

The courthouse is the one to look for. The current building dates from 1885 and was restored after a fire in 1934 destroyed its distinctive clock tower. The town was founded as Portersville in 1836 and renamed the following year, after Commodore David Porter's last battle off the Chilean port of Valparaíso.

The best starting point is Central Park Plaza, a grassy open space with walkways and storefronts on every side. It gives you a wide, relaxed view of the town with plenty of room to step back. The Orville Redenbacher statue at the plaza's north end makes a friendly foreground for a souvenir shot. Courthouse Square and the long view along Lincolnway are good alternatives once you have your first frames.

Keep the phone level so the building lines stay straight, and take a few frames at different distances. Look for details such as arched bank windows and stone pillars as well as the wide view.
text.geographic_location: In the centre of Valparaiso, Indiana, around the Porter County Courthouse square. The district runs between Jefferson, Morgan, Monroe and Napoleon Streets, and Central Park Plaza is about 150 m west of the centre of the district.
text.directions_text: No Underground, train or tram stops are listed for this spot, so head for the centre of Valparaiso, by taxi or hired scooter, and aim for the courthouse square. Walk east through the streets of old shopfronts and you will reach the square. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) to take in the plaza and the buildings around it, then use the default lens (1x) for a more natural look at the storefronts. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pick out courthouse and bank details from a distance.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Central Park Plaza (the open lawn and walkways, looking back toward the surrounding downtown buildings). A grassy open space with walkways, with the downtown storefronts and buildings surrounding it on every side. Out on the open lawn or along the walkways, and turn back to face the downtown buildings that surround it. From here you see grass and paths in front of you and the storefronts closing the frame on every side, with the centre of the district to the east.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and keep the horizon level, so the building edges stay upright. Use the paths as leading lines towards the buildings, and keep some lawn in the lower part of the frame. For a people shot, use portrait mode with the Orville Redenbacher statue at the north end of the plaza. For another view, try Courthouse Square for the courthouse framed by the old commercial blocks, or look down Lincolnway for a long view of the main street.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the buildings to set focus, then slide the exposure down a little if the sky is bright, so the stone and building fronts keep their colour. Try a panorama for the full sweep of the plaza, moving slowly and keeping the phone upright.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light on the fronts, and the plaza is often quieter earlier in the day.

text.access_note: Central Park Plaza is an open public park; check the official site before you go, as events can change how the plaza is set up.

label: Brauer Museum of Art

notes: Art museum on the Valparaiso University campus.

text.description:
The Brauer Museum of Art is the art museum of Valparaiso University, and it sits inside the university's Center for the Arts. Its collection covers 19th- and 20th-century American art, world religious art and Midwestern regional art, and it runs to over 2,700 pieces. It is named after Richard H. W. Brauer, the collection's long-time director and curator, and took his name in 1996. The museum closed in the summer of 2024 and reopened in November 2024.

For a phone photographer, the main picture here is the building itself: a calm arts-centre scene that works well as a record of your visit to the campus. Start with a wide shot of the entrance area so the building's name and setting are clear. Then step in for a few simpler frames, such as a doorway, a sign or a line of windows. If you go inside, photography rules can differ from gallery to gallery and exhibition to exhibition. Look for signs and ask a member of staff before taking pictures of artworks, and never use flash. Keep your phone steady against your body, and take two or three frames of each view so you can pick the sharpest later. The museum has held special exhibitions, so what is on show may change from one visit to the next.
text.geographic_location: On the campus of Valparaiso University in Valparaiso, Indiana, inside the university's Center for the Arts.
text.directions_text: The museum is part of the Valparaiso University Center for the Arts, on the university campus in Valparaiso, Indiana. Check the official Valparaiso University site for directions and parking, and look for the Center for the Arts on campus. The phone icon on the map is at the museum itself, so there is no extra walk once you arrive. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the building as you see it. Switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) if you are close and cannot fit the entrance in. Use the telephoto (2x or more, depending on your phone) for signs and architectural details.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. It is right at the museum, so the building is directly in front of you. Take one frame from here, then step back a few paces for a fuller view.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and line up the edges of the building with them so the walls look straight. Keep the phone level and leave a little space around the entrance. Then take a closer detail shot with the telephoto.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the building to focus. Then drag the exposure slider down a touch if the sky is bright, so the walls do not wash out. Indoors, check the photography rules first and turn the flash off.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Daytime in even light, such as a bright overcast day, gives clear, natural colours. Check the museum's visiting times on the official site before you go.

text.access_note: The museum is a university-run site, so access and photography rules may vary: check the official site before you go.
